o  INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, November 17, 2021, via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf called
the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  None

Public Comments

  Helen Lessick made a correction on page 2 of the September minutes where it reads ‘Crenshaw diary mart’ it
should read ‘Crenshaw Dairy Mart’.

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the minutes from September 15, 2021. Commissioner Battle
seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Lesure, Metcalf, Ehrlich-Bell, Battle and Banks
  Nays: None

Quarterly Report/Check-in Regarding HollywoodPark/Sofi Stadium Public Art

  Jason Witt, Director of Community Engagement from Hollywood Park/SoFi Stadium along with Tiffany Lendrum
gave a quarterly update regarding Hollywood Park/SoFi Stadium Public Art’s Hollywood Park Retail Art Program. Six (6)
murals will be installed throughout the retail area and two (2) sculptures in the Promenade area.

  Commissioner Lesure asked if they are in talks with artist Phil Bo. Ms. Lendrum stated he is aware. Commissioner
Metcalf stated she is excited and looks forward to hearing more about the Inglewood Artists.

  1
 o  INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  ARTS COMMISSION

Staff Report

  Helen Lessick introduced a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the Mayor and Council
Members deaccession the Kids of All Ages at North Park mural created by community members led by Anne Cheek La
Rose and Rezin (Ron Lewis) and preserve the project documentation in collection authority files.

  Director Barnes gave an overview of the mural which included:
  • 2012 Community project held at North Park for creative signage
  • Anne Cheek La Rose led community youth in painting shapes
  • Rezin leading Marriott International volunteers in painting a background
  • KaBOOM! Non-profit grant matched with City funds
  • Site modifications obscured mural sightlines
  • Ground-level perimeter path of a stone aggregate abrades mural

  Commissioner Battle asked if the mural will be removed and not replaced with anything. Director Barnes explained
the current mural doesn’t sit in a good place, something will replace it but it will not be Public Art. Commissioner Ehrlich-
Bell asked what happens to the existing art. Director Barnes stated due to the condition, it will be painted over.

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Ehrlich-Bell seconded and the staff
report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Lesure, Metcalf, Ehrlich-Bell, and Banks
  Abstained: Commissioner Battle
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Helen Lessick gave a verbal report regarding the following Public Art related projects:
  • Cleaning and conservation of five (5) exterior murals. All need cleaning and re-application of sacrificial
  coating; three (3) need minor repairs: faded paints need repainting. Murals are from 2010-2012 and
  have slim records of paint, pigments.
  • Rogers Park Artist in Residence (RPAiR) Shelley Heffler’s It Takes a Village Workshop Series 2 and
  January 2022 Exhibition. The final workshop series will be held from October 22, 2021, to December
  10, 2021. It will consist of a quilting workshop project held at the Rogers Park Community Center located
  at 400 W. Beach Avenue. on Fridays from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. and Saturday’s noon to 3:00 p.m. The
  workshop is free to registered participants. Registration can be done at www.Tinyurl.com/ITAVillage.
  The RPAiR Exhibition begins January 8, 2021, through February 26, 2022. Catalogs are available for
  purchase from the artist at a cost to produce. A final city report to the NEA will be completed by March
  30, 2022. Attendees are encouraged to complete our audience survey.
  • Inglewood Growing Artists Projects (IGAP) 2022/2023 program priorities and project opportunities,
  contract amounts ranging from $10,000 to $25,000 (1 or more projects) with a 12-month contract from
  the official notice to proceed. IGAP possibilities consist of:
  2
 o  INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  ARTS COMMISSION

  - Darby Park Artist in Residence:
  § The contracted artist to consider Darby Park as a public art canvas
  § Commission for a visual artist, sculptor, fabric artist, or writer
  § Possibility: Banner Project, visual artist or graphic designer working digitally
  - Inglewood Trees Artist:
  § The contracted artist considers Inglewood trees as public art content
  § City-wide exploration of Inglewood's public trees
  § Commission for a visual artist, poet, and/or creative non-fiction writer
  § Possibility: Hardcover book with imagery and texts

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  None

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:57 p.m.
